name: Quiet-work media reframing
description: The short media-label cycle that reframed fulfillment of contracted duties as a distinct workplace withdrawal practice.
cause_of_death: Rapid linguistic criticism followed adoption of the label; the underlying practice predates and outlasts the media cycle.

sources.title: The words and phrases to banish from your vocabulary in 2023
sources.note: Inspected contemporary report lists quiet quitting among phrases criticized for misuse, overuse and disconnection from literal meanings.

sources.title: Hustle culture: Is this the end of rise-and-grind?
sources.note: Reports diminished cultural aspiration after pandemic reprioritization; explicitly says the culture has not entirely faded and attests grindset.

entries.gloss: A label for fulfilling stated job requirements while withholding additional unpaid effort.

examples.text: I am quiet quitting the extra weekend work and will complete my assigned tasks on Monday.

entries.rationale: NPR documents quiet quitting as an overused phrase at the beginning of 2023; BBC identifies it as a replacement for rise-and-grind rhetoric in April 2023. The 2022 onset and peak, and 2025 fade, are estimated boundaries of its media-label moment rather than the underlying work practice. Continued usage is possible.
